Looking at each net, the four squares in a row wrap around to form the side faces of the cube, while the four triangular flaps (half‑squares) must pair up to cover the top and bottom faces exactly, with each pair of triangles forming complementary halves of a square face (matching along the same diagonal).

- **A:** Top flaps (squares 2,3) give SW + NE halves; bottom flaps give SW + NE halves. Complementary pairs — works.
- **B:** Top flaps give SW + NE; bottom flaps (squares 1,4) give SW + NE. Works.
- **C:** Top flaps (squares 1,4) give SW + NE — fine. But the bottom flaps: the flap on square 1 (right angle at left) covers the NW half, and the flap on square 4 (right angle at right) also covers the NW half. They **overlap**, leaving the SE half of the bottom face uncovered — fails.
- **D:** Top flaps give SW + NE; bottom flaps give NW + SE. Works.
- **E:** Top flaps give SW + NE; bottom flaps give SW + NE. Works.

Only net C has two triangular flaps that overlap instead of completing a face.

\boxed{C}
